# GEO report: orchard-site **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 100/100, Strong Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. Everything the rules check is in order, as read from code. This is a small Next.js site with 4 routes (`/`, `/varieties`, `/visit`, `/account`). Nothing was left unknown, apart from what only a running site or your CDN can show (see "Can't tell from code"). ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first Nothing is broken, so these are the biggest remaining unknowns and ideas. ### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your CDN or firewall - **Why it matters:** code can't show whether hosting protection blocks the search crawlers you want to allow. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100 if it comes back clear. The score doesn't change if it comes back a problem, because the code score only covers what's in the repo. The live result would be reported separately. ### 2. Make the Visit page deliver what its description promises - **Why it matters:** the description says "Opening times and directions", but the page has only one line of text, with no address or directions. Visitors and AI tools have nothing to quote. - **Where:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4` - **What the code says:** `

Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.

` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100 (no change, because this is an optional idea). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Matches `aiSearchCrawlers: allow`. Only GPTBot and ClaudeBot (training) are blocked, which matches your policy | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 public routes indexable. `/account` is noindex and not in the sitemap | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on own domain | Clear | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1` | | GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Server Components with static text | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, referenced at `public/robots.txt:11` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:5` (`lang="en"`). Each public page has a title and description. `/account` has no description but is noindex | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:7`, plain `` to all 3 public pages | | GEO-017 | No snippet conflict | Clear | Only scoped `data-nosnippet` (`app/layout.tsx:9`) | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read the layout and 4 pages. There are no images, and the links have text | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | Not present (information only) | | GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | Not an app | ## Other problems found None found. ## Worth considering - **Put the address and directions on /visit:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`: `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` The description promises directions, but the page has none. Add the address, directions and parking. - **Label the business with structured data:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`. No JSON-LD exists anywhere. Once the address and hours are on the page, add `LocalBusiness` (or `Organization`) JSON-LD with the same facts, so machines can read them without guessing. - **Name the site in a machine-readable way:** `app/layout.tsx:1`. Add `WebSite` and `Organization` JSON-LD with the name "Orchard" and the site URL you already use. - **Back up "Over forty varieties":** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` Only two are named. List the rest. - **Give each variety its own page:** same line. Pages like `/varieties/ashmeads-kernel` would be shareable and linkable, and they could be added to the sitemap. - **Link between pages in the text:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` The home page links onward only through the nav. Add links to Varieties and Visit in the body, and link "Herefordshire" to the directions. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://www.orchard.example/`. If you have real update dates, include them. A framework-generated `app/sitemap.ts` would keep it in sync as pages are added. - **Tell the home page's story:** `app/page.tsx:4`. The home page has two short lines. Say what you sell (trees, fruit, tours?), where you are and how to buy. - **Make the title and description more specific:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Visit the orchard'`. Name the orchard and place, e.g. "Visit Orchard, Herefordshire", so the title makes sense on its own in a result. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Server responses:** real status codes, redirects, and whether `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` answer 200 on the live host. These need a live check. - **Headers:** any `X-Robots-Tag` set at the CDN or host, outside the repository. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools to find the site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`. - `https://www.orchard.example` is the real origin, as declared in `geo.config.json`. - I read all 5 source files in `app/`, `public/robots.txt`, `public/sitemap.xml`, `package.json` and `geo.config.json`. That covers all 4 routes, the nav, the layout and the single robots and sitemap sources. I found no JSON-LD in the repository. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
